programs.title: A8 - Abenteuer Autobahn
programs.desc: For the fourth time we will have the opportunity to take a closer look at German expressways.The creators of the program take us to the A8 motorway.The 505-kilometer route starts in Perl, passes through Karlsruhe, Stuttgart, Augsburg and Munich, reaching all the way to the border with Austria.This road is one of the most important East-West connections in Central Europe.We will be able to see the work of the police, truck drivers, highway maintenance services, and engineers whose task is to smooth traffic.

programs.sub_title: Orange when you look at it!
programs.desc: Mechanics from the Fired Up workshop in Dallas, Texas, specialize in restoring old, classic cars and building unique hot rods to order.The team is celebrating its first year of operation.Thanks to the experience and prestige they have gained, the guys decide to take on truly ambitious projects.One of them is the restoration of a rare 1978 Chevrolet Blazer with two-wheel drive.Additionally, Thomas has the opportunity to purchase a highly sought-after 1963 Pontiac Grand Prix.

programs.title: Road absurdities 4
programs.desc:
In the next series, Kamil Jaśkowski and Krzysztof Ruszała continue their developing trips around Poland, during which they look for the causes of various absurd road solutions.Using a prototype siren with the mysterious symbol S201, they will go to places where officials lightly spent huge amounts of money on non-functional communication infrastructure facilities.A bicycle path with pedestrian crossings every few meters, a speed limit for only one lane, a "zebra" right behind the "parking" sign, poles at the entrances to the garage, a street lamp in the middle of the road - this is just the beginning of the list of topics that tireless hunters of road stupidity will face.
Kamil and Krzysiek will go to Tczew, where they will be stopped by a locked railway crossing.The presenters will also visit Sztum to see absurd road signs on the local bicycle path.In turn, when passing through Malbork, they will discover the "mayor's beret", i.e. a roundabout built on a straight road.Syrenka S201 will appear in Gdańsk, Ełk and Oława.Finally, a short visit to Warsaw: on the grounds of the National Stadium and at an unused bus stop built for about thirty thousand zlotys.

programs.title: Road absurdities 4
programs.desc:
In the next series, Kamil Jaśkowski and Krzysztof Ruszała continue their developing trips around Poland, during which they look for the causes of various absurd road solutions.Using a prototype siren with the mysterious symbol S201, they will go to places where officials lightly spent huge amounts of money on non-functional communication infrastructure facilities.A bicycle path with pedestrian crossings every few meters, a speed limit for only one lane, a "zebra" right behind the "parking" sign, poles at the entrances to the garage, a street lamp in the middle of the road - this is just the beginning of the list of topics that tireless hunters of road stupidity will face.
While tracking down road absurdities, the leaders will be in Bielawa and Oleśnica.In Wrocław they will be surprised by traffic lights that glow only orange, and in Syców they will be surprised by completely unnecessary road signs.In turn, in Tczew, Kamil and Krzysiek will cross a pedestrian crossing leading to a 25-centimeter-wide sidewalk.The crew of Syrenka S201 will also solve the mystery of the tonnage limitation in Łeba.Finally, there will be a ride along the Warsaw fire road and examination of the intersection at Sokolej Street.
